---
title: "A time series that draws itself"
description: "transition_reveal() grows four stock-index lines along a Date column, with a smoothly advancing leading point and the date reached so far in the title."
categories: [Animation]
image: figs/reveal-timeseries-poster.png
---



`transition_states()` and `transition_time()` move marks between states.
`transition_reveal()` does something else: it draws the data *in*, in the order of a
variable. Each frame shows the rows reached so far, and a line grows through them with
an interpolated leading point, so it advances smoothly between observations rather
than jumping from one to the next.

The data is R's `EuStockMarkets`, daily closing prices of four European indices from
1991 to 1998, thinned to one trading day in five and given real `Date`s.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
step <- seq(1, nrow(EuStockMarkets), by = 5)
days <- as.Date("1991-01-01") +
  round((as.numeric(time(EuStockMarkets))[step] - 1991) * 365.25)

stocks <- data.frame(
  date  = rep(days, 4),
  index = rep(colnames(EuStockMarkets), each = length(step)),
  close = as.vector(EuStockMarkets[step, ])
)

range(stocks$date)
#> [1] "1991-07-01" "1998-08-19"
```
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
a <- vplot(stocks, width = 7, height = 3.6) |>
  mark_line(x = date, y = close, color = index) |>
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") |>
  labs(title = "European stock indices, {format(frame_along, '%B %Y')}",
       x = NULL, y = "closing price") |>
  transition_reveal(date) |>
  animate(nframes = 120, fps = 20)
```
:::



::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](figs/reveal-timeseries.svg){width=100%}
:::
:::


The 120 frames are spread evenly over the range of `date`, from July 1991 to August
1998. The title uses the frame variable `{frame_along}`, the `along` value reached by
the frame, which keeps the class of the column: here a `Date`, so `format()` with a
`strftime` pattern turns it into a month and a year. Any R expression works inside the
braces.

Only the data layers are revealed. The panel, gridlines, axes and legend are drawn
whole on every frame, and the scales are trained once over all the data and frozen,
so the y axis already reaches 8 000 in 1991, and the late-1990s run-up is drawn
against the same axis as the flat early years. A yearly break with a `"%Y"` label keeps
the date axis to seven short labels.

## Size

Each frame carries the lines revealed so far, so the file grows with the length of the
series times the number of frames: here about 2 MB of SVG, around 40 KB once the server
compresses it. Thinning a daily series to weekly, as above, is the main lever; a
smaller `nframes` is the other.
